target_customer: Card issuers, banks, neobanks and fintechs that pay for verified merchant data on transactions
problem: Raw card and bank transaction strings are messy, so issuers cannot reliably tell who and where a payment was with, which hurts fraud decisions, rewards and customer service.
business_model: API and data platform sold to financial institutions (usage and contract based, pricing not public)
product_category: Transaction enrichment and merchant intelligence data platform

founders.name: Oban MacTavish
previous_startups: Hubly (vertical SaaS for independent RIAs, co-founder)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-founded Hubly. One podcast summary says consulting with fintechs led him to start Spade in November 2021. Education not found.

founders.name: Cooper Hart
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch (2023-02-27) as a founder with Oban MacTavish. Not on the YC page. Background not found.

founders.name: Tess Bloch
founders.role: Co-founder, operations, finance, sales and people
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a TechCrunch photo caption (2023-12-06) and a podcast summary. Not on the YC page. Background not found.

competitors.name: Heron Data
competitors.what: Transaction and bank data enrichment for fintechs, a YC Summer 2020 company

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a ground truth merchant database with human labeling plus a real-time API under 50 ms for issuers needed solid data engineering and operations, but not research-grade work.

defensibility.rationale: The verified merchant database compounds with coverage and sits inside issuer authorization flows, though competitors such as Ntropy, Heron and Plaid sold enrichment too.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Plaid and others bundled enrichment features, but Spade stayed independent, signed a Stripe Issuing partnership and raised three rounds through 2026-03.

market_need_then: Fintech and issuer demand for merchant enrichment was visible by 2021 through startups such as Heron (2020) and Ntropy, and issuers needed better data for fraud and rewards. Direct demand metrics at 2021 were not found.

branding.domain_note: Now uses spade.com, an exact match domain; acquisition history not found

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and data infrastructure oriented, now framed as data and AI platform for modern finance

branding.community_and_virality: Founders appear on fintech podcasts and TechCrunch coverage, but no merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name, exact .com, and steady trade press, but no sourced evidence of brand driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Spade is a growth stage company of about 30 people that raised a 5 million seed from a16z in 2023-02, a 10 million Series A in 2023-12 and a 40 million Series B in 2026-03. Its hand labeled merchant database, API partnerships such as Stripe and named customers like Mercury and Bilt support its position, and the company reports 470 percent year over year growth. Rivals Ntropy and Heron offer enrichment, so the data moat is the key variable.
notes: TechCrunch says the seed brought total raised to 6.1 million USD, so about 1.1 million came earlier (likely YC and pre-seed) and is not itemized. One listing dates the seed to 2022-09 or shows a 6.1 million seed in 2022-05, conflicting with the company blog and TechCrunch (2023-02). Series B is confirmed by Business Wire, FinTech Global and Oak HC/FT. Ntropy raised a Series A in 2022-10 (after the batch) and is a later-dated rival, not listed. Aggregators list customers Stripe, Bilt and Mercury; only Bilt, Coast and Mercury are confirmed on the company site.
